# Rebase Documentation

> Rebase is an open-source TypeScript backend built on Postgres: a REST API, authentication,
> row-level security, realtime subscriptions, storage, cron jobs, and an MCP server for AI agents —
> all generated from your schema, with a full admin panel and SQL editor included on top.
> Connect an existing PostgreSQL database or start fresh; Rebase uses Drizzle ORM under the hood and
> keeps your TypeScript collection definitions as the single source of truth.
> Scoped API keys with per-collection permissions plus Postgres-enforced RLS make it safe for
> autonomous agents to read and write production data.

## Product

- [Rebase](https://rebase.pro/): What Rebase is: a Postgres backend with an admin panel generated from the same schema.
- [Backend](https://rebase.pro/backend): The backend on its own — REST API, auth, RLS, realtime, storage, functions, cron.
- [Admin panel (Studio)](https://rebase.pro/studio): The admin UI your non-technical teammates use, generated from the collections.
- [Pricing](https://rebase.pro/pricing): Open source and self-hosted, plus Rebase Cloud (private beta), priced per resource rather than per seat.
- [Security](https://rebase.pro/security): Row-level security compiled from code to real Postgres policies, and how it is enforced.
- [rls-check (free tool)](https://rebase.pro/rls-check): A free, read-only Row-Level Security audit for ANY Postgres database — Supabase, Neon, RDS, anything. 15 checks, one command, no account, no Rebase required.
- [For agencies](https://rebase.pro/agencies): Shipping a client-ready admin panel from the backend you were going to build anyway.
- [CLI](https://rebase.pro/cli): `npm i -g @rebasepro/cli` — scaffold, run, migrate and deploy a project.
- [Compare](https://rebase.pro/compare): Side-by-side against the alternatives, including where a competitor is the better call.

## Documentation

- [Introduction](https://rebase.pro/docs/index.md): Rebase is the open-source backend for Postgres, with an admin panel for your team, built with React and TypeScript. Define your schema in TypeScript, and Rebase generates a full CRUD UI, REST API, authentication, storage, and real-time sync — powered by PostgreSQL.
- [Quickstart](https://rebase.pro/docs/getting-started/quickstart.md): Create a new Rebase project and get it running locally in under 2 minutes.
- [Project Structure](https://rebase.pro/docs/getting-started/project-structure.md): Understand the structure of a Rebase project — frontend, backend, and collections configuration.
- [Environment & Configuration](https://rebase.pro/docs/getting-started/configuration.md): All environment variables and configuration options for Rebase projects.
- [Troubleshooting](https://rebase.pro/docs/troubleshooting.md): The failures that stop a Rebase backend from starting or serving — an unreachable database, wrong credentials, a missing extension, an RLS refusal, schema drift, a busy port, a function that will not load — and what each one looks like.
- [Upgrading](https://rebase.pro/docs/upgrading.md): What breaks when you move an existing app to the current release, and what to do about each one.
- [Upgrading 0.29 to 0.30](https://rebase.pro/docs/upgrading/0-29-to-0-30.md): The breaking changes 0.30 carries for an app on 0.29 — a backend booted with initializeRebaseBackend keeps the refresh token in a cookie by default.
- [Upgrading 0.27 to 0.29](https://rebase.pro/docs/upgrading/0-27-to-0-29.md): The breaking changes 0.29 carries for an app on 0.27 or 0.28 — the admin hands your code the server's rows instead of its internal Entity, its Entity hooks go internal, and "which record" is `id` everywhere.
- [Upgrading 0.26 to 0.27](https://rebase.pro/docs/upgrading/0-26-to-0-27.md): The breaking changes 0.27 carries for an app on 0.26 — cron schedules that restrict both day fields, malformed cron numbers, a key strategy its type cannot honour, managed deploys that stop on a file that did not load, and browser clients that default to cookie auth.
- [Upgrading 0.25 to 0.26](https://rebase.pro/docs/upgrading/0-25-to-0-26.md): The breaking changes 0.26 carries for an app on 0.25 — multi-hop via writes, role names, storage page tokens, the functions upstream, OAuth refusal reasons, the MCP server's app key, generated foreign keys, and three cloud commands and tokens.
- [Upgrading 0.24 to 0.25](https://rebase.pro/docs/upgrading/0-24-to-0-25.md): The breaking changes 0.25 carries for an app on 0.24 — the REST count switch, the MCP collection listing, the admin's translations, stricter refusals at boot and on writes and reads, the SDK's cron path and offline reads, storage sources, the UI kit, session length and the password policy, and removed exports.
- [Upgrading 0.23 to 0.24](https://rebase.pro/docs/upgrading/0-23-to-0-24.md): The breaking changes 0.24 carries for an app on 0.23 — generated SQL and SDK types, CLI paths, scopes, upserts and keys, the remote MCP endpoint, sessions and accounts, the backup routes, the insights plugin and images in markdown fields.
- [Upgrading 0.21 to 0.23](https://rebase.pro/docs/upgrading/0-21-to-0-23.md): The breaking changes 0.23 carries for an app on 0.21 or 0.22 — nested-path API keys, boot refusals, custom auth repositories, guest upgrades and custom job stores.
- [Upgrading 0.18 to 0.21](https://rebase.pro/docs/upgrading/0-18-to-0-21.md): Every breaking change in 0.21, and what to do about each one.
- [Upgrading 0.17 to 0.18](https://rebase.pro/docs/upgrading/0-17-to-0-18.md): Every breaking change in 0.18, and what to do about each one.
- [Upgrading 0.14 to 0.17](https://rebase.pro/docs/upgrading/0-14-to-0-17.md): The admin package renames, declared resources, and the bundle format change that stops an older build booting on a current runtime.
- [Upgrading 0.13 to 0.14](https://rebase.pro/docs/upgrading/0-13-to-0-14.md): Every wire key becomes camelCase, anonymous sign-in becomes opt-in, and one package is removed.
- [Upgrading 0.12 to 0.13](https://rebase.pro/docs/upgrading/0-12-to-0-13.md): The auth schema removal, the package renames, and the three ways access could be granted that you did not ask for.
- [Compatibility](https://rebase.pro/docs/compatibility.md): What Rebase promises across versions and what it does not — the six versioned contracts, how each one fails, and what may still change in a minor.
- [Changelog](https://rebase.pro/docs/changelog.md): Every released change to Rebase — new features, fixes, and the breaking changes each version asks you to migrate.
- [Backend only (headless)](https://rebase.pro/docs/getting-started/headless.md): Run Rebase as a headless Backend-as-a-Service over your own PostgreSQL — a REST API, auth, storage and realtime, with no admin panel and no collection files.
- [Running on an existing or shared database](https://rebase.pro/docs/deployment/existing-database.md): Run Rebase on a PostgreSQL database it does not own — a cluster shared with other apps, a second Rebase project, Supabase, or a database a DBA locks down — with the rls settings, rebase doctor --database and rebase db request-role migrate.
- [REST API](https://rebase.pro/docs/backend/api.md): Auto-generated REST API endpoints for every collection, with filtering, sorting, pagination, and relation inclusion.
- [REST API filtering](https://rebase.pro/docs/backend/filtering.md): Filter REST list requests with PostgREST-style operators, or/and groups and the where JSON dialect, and see how the filters combine.
- [Writing over REST](https://rebase.pro/docs/backend/writes.md): Idempotency keys, conditional writes with ETag and If-Match, field operations, upserts on a natural key, return=minimal, and cross-collection batches.
- [Typed SDK — Getting Started](https://rebase.pro/docs/sdk.md): Install and configure the Rebase typed SDK to interact with your backend from any JavaScript or TypeScript application.
- [Security Rules (RLS)](https://rebase.pro/docs/collections/security-rules.md): Define Row Level Security policies for your collections using convenience shortcuts or raw SQL expressions.
- [Field access](https://rebase.pro/docs/collections/field-access.md): Per-property read and write permissions by role. A caller the row's security rules let through still does not receive a field their roles cannot read.
- [Tenancy](https://rebase.pro/docs/collections/tenancy.md): Scope every row of a collection to a site, organization or workspace with one declaration, enforced by Postgres row-level security.
- [Collections](https://rebase.pro/docs/collections.md): Collections are the core building block of Rebase — each collection maps to a database table and defines its schema, relations, security, and UI behavior.
- [Properties](https://rebase.pro/docs/collections/properties.md): Property types define the data type, validation, and UI rendering for each field in a collection. Rebase supports string, number, boolean, date, array, map, reference, relation, and geopoint types.
- [Arrays and maps](https://rebase.pro/docs/collections/arrays-and-maps.md): The two composite property types: repeatable lists, block editors, structured groups and free-form key-value objects, and how each maps to a Postgres column.
- [File upload fields](https://rebase.pro/docs/collections/file-uploads.md): Declaring a file or image field on a collection: the storage block, single and multi-file uploads, and which of its options the panel resolves rather than the server.
- [Validation and conditions](https://rebase.pro/docs/collections/validation-and-conditions.md): Enum values, per-property validation rules, and the conditional fields that make a property required, disabled or hidden based on the entity's own values.
- [Relations](https://rebase.pro/docs/collections/relations.md): Define one-to-one, one-to-many, and many-to-many SQL relations between collections with foreign keys, junction tables, and multi-hop joins.
- [Relations in the admin panel](https://rebase.pro/docs/collections/relations-in-the-admin-panel.md): How every to-many relation becomes a tab under a record — the path segment, owned versus shared rows, the same rules over REST, and what does not become a tab.
- [Soft delete](https://rebase.pro/docs/collections/soft-delete.md): Turn delete into a timestamp, hide stamped rows from every read, and restore them with an ordinary update.
- [Views](https://rebase.pro/docs/collections/views.md): Serve a SQL view or materialized view as a read-only collection, declared in config and created by db push.
- [Entity Callbacks](https://rebase.pro/docs/collections/callbacks.md): Use lifecycle callbacks to run custom logic when entities are created, updated, read, or deleted. Includes the context.data API for cross-collection operations.
- [The context.data API](https://rebase.pro/docs/collections/context-data-api.md): Read and write other collections from inside a callback with context.data — its methods, the privileges it runs with, transaction semantics, and the connection a callback holds.
- [Security Rules (RLS)](https://rebase.pro/docs/collections/security-rules.md): Define Row Level Security policies for your collections using convenience shortcuts or raw SQL expressions.
- [Field access](https://rebase.pro/docs/collections/field-access.md): Per-property read and write permissions by role. A caller the row's security rules let through still does not receive a field their roles cannot read.
- [Tenancy](https://rebase.pro/docs/collections/tenancy.md): Scope every row of a collection to a site, organization or workspace with one declaration, enforced by Postgres row-level security.
- [Backend Overview](https://rebase.pro/docs/backend.md): The Rebase backend provides a complete server with REST API, authentication, storage, WebSocket real-time, and entity history — all initialized with a single function call.
- [Rebase doesn't do X](https://rebase.pro/docs/backend/extending.md): The server-side extension ladder — declaration, collection callback, custom function, your own routes, your own server, eject — with what each one can and cannot reach.
- [REST API](https://rebase.pro/docs/backend/api.md): Auto-generated REST API endpoints for every collection, with filtering, sorting, pagination, and relation inclusion.
- [REST API filtering](https://rebase.pro/docs/backend/filtering.md): Filter REST list requests with PostgREST-style operators, or/and groups and the where JSON dialect, and see how the filters combine.
- [Writing over REST](https://rebase.pro/docs/backend/writes.md): Idempotency keys, conditional writes with ETag and If-Match, field operations, upserts on a natural key, return=minimal, and cross-collection batches.
- [API keys](https://rebase.pro/docs/backend/api-keys.md): Long-lived keys for scripts, CI, agents and integrations: service keys and personal keys, the scopes they hold, how they compose with row-level security, and the routes that manage them.
- [Error codes](https://rebase.pro/docs/backend/errors.md): Every error code a Rebase backend can return, with its HTTP status, what it means and what to do about it — plus the response envelope, X-Request-ID and the details rules.
- [Endpoint index](https://rebase.pro/docs/backend/endpoints.md): Every HTTP route a Rebase backend mounts — data, auth, storage, admin, meta — with the gate on each one and the page that explains it.
- [Live schema editing](https://rebase.pro/docs/backend/live-schema-editing.md): Create and alter collections against a running backend — committed to your repository first, then applied.
- [Authentication](https://rebase.pro/docs/backend/authentication.md): Configure JWT authentication, OAuth providers, SMTP email, bot protection and the users collection on the Rebase backend.
- [Roles and scopes](https://rebase.pro/docs/backend/roles-and-scopes.md): What a caller may do: the data plane every person holds, the admin plane that roles grant, the scopes an app declares for itself, and how each credential carries them.
- [Email verification](https://rebase.pro/docs/backend/email-verification.md): How an account proves its email address: the link mailed at registration, what following it keeps and removes, and confirm-first registration with requireEmailVerification.
- [Device sign-in](https://rebase.pro/docs/backend/device-sign-in.md): Let a terminal or another device without a browser sign in through one: a short code, a link, and an approval by a signed-in user. RFC 8628's device authorization grant, as rebase cloud login uses it.
- [Auth endpoints and tokens](https://rebase.pro/docs/backend/auth-endpoints.md): The authentication routes the Rebase backend mounts, their response shapes, multi-factor authentication, the database context a policy sees, JWKS and service keys.
- [Custom auth adapters](https://rebase.pro/docs/backend/auth-adapters.md): Replace Rebase's built-in authentication with Clerk, Firebase Auth or your own identity provider by implementing the AuthAdapter contract.
- [Storage Configuration](https://rebase.pro/docs/backend/storage.md): Configure local filesystem, S3-compatible, or GCS/Firebase Storage backends for file uploads, images, and media.
- [Storage Authorization](https://rebase.pro/docs/backend/storage-authorization.md): Decide who may read, write, delete or list each storage object with storagePolicies and the storageAuthorize hook, and which storage scopes an API key needs.
- [Storage caching and CDNs](https://rebase.pro/docs/backend/storage-caching.md): How Rebase serves stored files so browsers and CDNs can cache them — ETags and 304s, Cache-Control by who may read an object, byte ranges for seeking in audio and video, and what to configure on a CDN in front.
- [Resumable uploads (TUS)](https://rebase.pro/docs/backend/storage-resumable-uploads.md): The TUS v1.0.0 endpoint under /api/storage/tus — how a large file goes up a chunk at a time, what each request answers, how the SDK and the admin panel use it, and how it behaves across restarts and instances.
- [Multiple Databases and Buckets](https://rebase.pro/docs/backend/multiple-sources.md): Route collections to different databases and properties to different storage buckets, and configure each one from the environment.
- [MongoDB](https://rebase.pro/docs/backend/mongodb.md): @rebasepro/server-mongo runs Rebase on MongoDB: a complete data driver, change-stream realtime and snapshot history — and no row-level security.
- [Realtime & WebSocket](https://rebase.pro/docs/backend/realtime.md): Real-time data synchronization, broadcast channels, and presence tracking via WebSocket.
- [Realtime across instances](https://rebase.pro/docs/backend/realtime-transports.md): How broadcast channels and presence survive more than one server process: the LISTEN/NOTIFY bus, what each instance owns, and writing your own transport.
- [Database change capture](https://rebase.pro/docs/backend/realtime-cdc.md): Realtime events for every committed write, however it was made: the capture triggers, the REALTIME_CDC setting, and what they need.
- [Search](https://rebase.pro/docs/backend/search.md): How .search() behaves by default, and how to opt a Postgres collection in to ranked full-text search over the fields you name — including JSONB and array content.
- [Vector Search](https://rebase.pro/docs/backend/vector-search.md): Nearest-neighbour search over a vector property through the REST API — the query parameters, thresholds, embeddings too long for a URL, and how filters behave on an HNSW index.
- [Indexes](https://rebase.pro/docs/backend/indexes.md): Declare ordinary Postgres indexes on a collection — btree, GIN and BRIN, partial, composite, covering and unique — and why a hand-written one used to disappear.
- [Cron Jobs](https://rebase.pro/docs/backend/cron-jobs.md): Schedule recurring background tasks with Rebase's built-in cron job system. Define jobs as TypeScript files, monitor them in Studio, and manage them via the REST API.
- [Cron Jobs API](https://rebase.pro/docs/backend/cron-jobs-api.md): List, trigger, pause and resume cron jobs over the REST API, or with the typed SDK's client.cron.
- [Cron across instances](https://rebase.pro/docs/backend/cron-across-instances.md): How cron jobs behave with more than one server process: one run per slot, a slot a restart dropped, a pause every replica honours, and runs that never overlap.
- [Background Jobs](https://rebase.pro/docs/backend/jobs.md): A durable, Postgres-backed job queue — work that survives a restart, retried with backoff, with failures kept rather than dropped.
- [Custom Functions](https://rebase.pro/docs/backend/custom-functions.md): Add custom Hono API endpoints alongside your Rebase CRUD routes. Auto-discovered from a directory, with full access to the backend instance.
- [Background Work](https://rebase.pro/docs/backend/background-work.md): Run work after a custom function has answered: waitUntil, what the host does with it at shutdown, and what is lost without it.
- [Runtime portability](https://rebase.pro/docs/backend/runtime-portability.md): What a custom function imports decides whether it could run outside a Node process — what is portable, what is Node-only, and how rebase build and rebase doctor report it.
- [Typed server-side data](https://rebase.pro/docs/backend/typed-server-data.md): Register your generated Database type once, and context.data, rebase.dataAsAdmin and the rebase a function or cron receives are typed from it: rows, filters, sorts, includes and write inputs.
- [Global Backend Hooks](https://rebase.pro/docs/backend/hooks.md): Apply cross-cutting lifecycle callbacks to every collection at the server level using CollectionCallbacks.
- [Entity History](https://rebase.pro/docs/backend/history.md): Track every change to your entities with a full audit trail — who changed what, when, and the complete before/after entity.
- [Database Branching](https://rebase.pro/docs/backend/branching.md): Create isolated database branches for development, staging, and testing using PostgreSQL's CREATE DATABASE ... TEMPLATE — instant, full-fidelity copies with zero downtime.
- [Custom Server Integration](https://rebase.pro/docs/backend/custom-server.md): Build the Rebase backend from public pieces in your own server — createRebaseBackend, its route groups, mount, attachRealtime and start — or embed the Postgres driver in Express.
- [Embedding the Postgres Driver](https://rebase.pro/docs/backend/embedding-postgres-driver.md): Open @rebasepro/server-postgres's data driver and realtime socket inside Express, Fastify or plain Node, without the Rebase server — read replicas, Drizzle and draining included.
- [Scripts and the Console](https://rebase.pro/docs/backend/scripts.md): Open a project's data from a script, a test or a REPL with openRebase, or from the terminal with rebase console. No server, no schema changes.
- [Frontend Overview](https://rebase.pro/docs/frontend.md): Build and customize the panel — Rebase CMS and Rebase Studio — with React: controllers, scaffold, routing, and views.
- [Customizing the Admin](https://rebase.pro/docs/frontend/customizing.md): How to customize the Rebase admin — building blocks, hooks and places, with tested recipes for singletons, per-user settings, bulk actions, calendar views, dashboards and custom login screens.
- [Panels in a page of your own](https://rebase.pro/docs/frontend/panels.md): Show one collection, one record's form, one record or one value in a page of your own: CollectionPanel, RecordForm, RecordDetail, FieldValue and CollectionsProvider, with no admin shell around them.
- [Extending Rebase](https://rebase.pro/docs/frontend/extending.md): A decision guide for choosing the right extension mechanism — plugins, slots, component overrides, entity views, actions, and more.
- [Styling Custom UI](https://rebase.pro/docs/frontend/styling.md): Build custom views, home pages and actions out of the same components and theme tokens as the rest of the admin, so they look native and follow the theme.
- [Translations](https://rebase.pro/docs/frontend/i18n.md): Change any string in the Rebase admin, add a language, or read the current locale from your own components.
- [Component Overrides (Swizzling)](https://rebase.pro/docs/frontend/component-overrides.md): Override default UI components with custom implementations at the application or collection level.
- [Authentication & Login](https://rebase.pro/docs/frontend/authentication.md): Set up the auth controller, login view, and role simulation in your Rebase React frontend.
- [Storage & File Uploads](https://rebase.pro/docs/frontend/storage.md): Add file upload fields to your collections, manage files programmatically, and route uploads to different storage backends.
- [View Modes](https://rebase.pro/docs/frontend/view-modes.md): Configure table, cards, and Kanban board views for your collections.
- [Firebase](https://rebase.pro/docs/frontend/firebase.md): @rebasepro/firebase runs Rebase CMS against Firestore, Firebase Auth and Firebase Storage — a client-side adapter, with no Rebase server involved.
- [Custom Fields](https://rebase.pro/docs/frontend/custom-fields.md): Build custom form fields for entity editing with full access to the form context, entity values, and Rebase hooks.
- [Form Layout](https://rebase.pro/docs/frontend/form-layout.md): Control how the entity form is arranged — column spans, sections, and the metadata rail.
- [Entity Views](https://rebase.pro/docs/frontend/entity-views.md): Add custom tabs and views to entity detail pages for previews, analytics, related data, or custom UI.
- [Entity Actions](https://rebase.pro/docs/frontend/entity-actions.md): Add custom action buttons to entities for archiving, publishing, exporting, cloning, and more.
- [Additional Columns](https://rebase.pro/docs/frontend/additional-columns.md): Add computed/virtual columns to collection tables that derive values from entity data.
- [Slots](https://rebase.pro/docs/frontend/slots.md): Reference for all UI extension point slots available in Rebase — named locations where you can inject custom components.
- [Data Import & Export](https://rebase.pro/docs/frontend/data-import-export.md): Import data from CSV, JSON, and Excel files into your collections, and export collection data to CSV or JSON with optional computed fields.
- [Plugin System](https://rebase.pro/docs/plugins.md): Extend Rebase with plugins — inject UI components, modify collections, add toolbar actions, and create custom field builders.
- [Hooks Reference](https://rebase.pro/docs/hooks.md): React hooks provided by Rebase for accessing auth, data, navigation, side panels, storage, and UI state.
- [Studio Tools](https://rebase.pro/docs/studio.md): Rebase Studio provides developer tools for visual schema editing, SQL queries, JavaScript scripting, RLS policy management, and storage browsing.
- [Components](https://rebase.pro/docs/ui/components.md): Components in @rebasepro/ui — the component library Rebase CMS and Rebase Studio are built from.

- [Typed SDK — Getting Started](https://rebase.pro/docs/sdk.md): Install and configure the Rebase typed SDK to interact with your backend from any JavaScript or TypeScript application.
- [Querying Data](https://rebase.pro/docs/sdk/querying.md): CRUD operations, fluent query builder, filter operators, sorting, column selection and aggregates with the Rebase typed SDK.
- [Pagination](https://rebase.pro/docs/sdk/pagination.md): Page a collection with limit/offset, page numbers, or a keyset cursor — and when each one stops being correct.
- [Writing data](https://rebase.pro/docs/sdk/writing.md): create, upsert, update and delete with the SDK — field operations, conditional writes, idempotency keys, batch writes, and writing across collections in one transaction.
- [Aggregates and search](https://rebase.pro/docs/sdk/aggregates-and-search.md): Count, sum and group with the SDK, filter inside JSON columns, and run full-text and vector search from the client.
- [Querying relations](https://rebase.pro/docs/sdk/relations.md): Include related entities in a query, and read a child collection through its parent with the SDK's relation accessors.
- [Authentication](https://rebase.pro/docs/sdk/authentication.md): Client-side authentication with the Rebase SDK — email/password sign-in, OAuth providers, session management, and auth state listeners.
- [Multi-Factor Authentication](https://rebase.pro/docs/sdk/multi-factor-authentication.md): TOTP factors with the Rebase SDK: enrolling one, the second step of a sign-in, recovery codes, and removing a factor.
- [Your Own Auth Provider](https://rebase.pro/docs/sdk/your-own-auth-provider.md): Authenticating the Rebase SDK with a provider of your own — Clerk, Firebase Auth or an existing session — through a token getter, over HTTP and the realtime socket.
- [Realtime Subscriptions](https://rebase.pro/docs/sdk/realtime.md): Subscribe to live data changes with the Rebase typed SDK using WebSocket-based realtime listeners.
- [Offline & Local-First Sync](https://rebase.pro/docs/sdk/offline.md): Enable the Rebase typed SDK's local-first sync engine — a local row database, instant offline writes with rollback, and reactive live queries.
- [Storage & Files](https://rebase.pro/docs/sdk/storage.md): Upload, download, list, and delete files using the Rebase typed SDK's storage module.
- [AI & Agents](https://rebase.pro/docs/ai.md): What Rebase ships for AI coding assistants and autonomous agents — an MCP server, project-local agent skills, scaffolded instruction files, and the credential model that decides what an agent can actually reach.
- [MCP Server](https://rebase.pro/docs/ai/mcp.md): Connect Claude Code, Cursor, Gemini CLI or any MCP client to a Rebase project — the 53 tools it exposes, the credential it authenticates with, and the loopback gate that stands between an agent and production.
- [MCP tool reference](https://rebase.pro/docs/ai/mcp-tool-reference.md): Every tool the Rebase MCP server registers, by group — what each one needs and does, and which ones the loopback gate refuses against a non-local project.
- [The Remote MCP Endpoint](https://rebase.pro/docs/ai/remote-mcp.md): Serve MCP from a deployed backend at /mcp, so the people who use your app can connect Claude or Cursor as themselves — OAuth with a consent screen, seventeen tools under three scopes, every call under their own row-level security.
- [Connect Claude to Rebase](https://rebase.pro/docs/ai/rebase-connector.md): One MCP connector for all your Rebase projects, on Rebase Cloud or self-hosted — add it once in Claude, sign in with your Rebase account, and read, deploy and change your projects with the access you have in the console, every change confirmed first.
- [Agent Skills](https://rebase.pro/docs/ai/skills.md): rebase skills install writes 24 Rebase reference skills into your repo, in the layout your AI assistant expects — Cursor, Claude Code, Windsurf, Gemini CLI and Antigravity.
- [AI Instruction Files](https://rebase.pro/docs/ai/instruction-files.md): Every scaffolded Rebase project ships ai-instructions.md plus pointer files for Claude, Cursor, Windsurf, Copilot and AGENTS.md that carry the five rules assistants break most — one source of truth, many filenames.
- [CLI Reference](https://rebase.pro/docs/cli.md): Rebase CLI commands for project initialization, schema generation, database migrations, and SDK generation.
- [Database Commands](https://rebase.pro/docs/cli/database.md): The rebase db commands — push, generate and migrate, backups and restores, pulling a copy, the connection string, the managed development database, and branches.
- [rebase cloud](https://rebase.pro/docs/cli/cloud.md): The command groups for Rebase Cloud in the CLI — auth, project link, deploys, notifications, config, organizations, databases, resources, compute, storage, clusters, billing and usage.
- [Schema Generation](https://rebase.pro/docs/cli/schema.md): Generate Drizzle ORM schemas from collection definitions, create SQL migrations, and keep your database in sync with the Rebase CLI.
- [rls-check](https://rebase.pro/docs/rls-check.md): Audit row-level security on any PostgreSQL database — Supabase, Neon, RDS, or your own server. Read-only, no signup, no Rebase required.
- [Architecture Overview](https://rebase.pro/docs/architecture.md): Understand how Rebase's backend, frontend, typed SDK, and database integrate to form a complete Backend-as-a-Service.
- [Schema as Code](https://rebase.pro/docs/architecture/schema-as-code.md): How Rebase uses TypeScript collections as the single source of truth for your database schema, UI, and API.
- [Runtime and Bundles](https://rebase.pro/docs/architecture/runtime-and-bundles.md): How a Rebase project separates into a project bundle and a versioned runtime, and why that separation is what makes upgrades, multi-repo apps and managed hosting possible.
- [Apps and Repositories](https://rebase.pro/docs/architecture/apps-and-repositories.md): A project is a backend plus the apps that talk to it, which can each live in their own repository.
- [Deployment](https://rebase.pro/docs/deployment.md): Where a Rebase project can run — Rebase Cloud, your own server, Kubernetes, or a managed container platform — and which guide to open for each.
- [Deployment](https://rebase.pro/docs/getting-started/deployment.md): Deploy your Rebase project to production using Docker, cloud platforms, or manual setups.
- [Rebase Cloud](https://rebase.pro/docs/deployment/cloud.md): Rebase Cloud is the same Rebase, operated for you. What it is, how a project links and deploys, and what the private beta does not include yet.
- [CI, Agents and Claimable Backends](https://rebase.pro/docs/deployment/cloud-agents.md): Deploy to Rebase Cloud from CI or an agent with a scoped token instead of a password, and let an agent provision a live backend with no account that a person claims later.
- [Cloud Notifications](https://rebase.pro/docs/deployment/cloud-notifications.md): How Rebase Cloud tells people when a deploy fails, backups stop, a payment is declined or usage passes 80% — signed webhooks to Slack, Discord or any URL, and per-person email.
- [Managed backend runtime](https://rebase.pro/docs/deployment/managed-runtime.md): What a backend with runtime "managed" can and cannot do on Rebase Cloud — packages and binaries, memory and CPU, timeouts and body sizes, the filesystem, in-memory state, secrets, storage for generated files, and outbound network.
- [Self-Hosting](https://rebase.pro/docs/deployment/self-hosting.md): Run Rebase anywhere with the official runtime image and your project bundle — Docker Compose, Fly, Railway, or a plain VPS.
- [Splitting into several processes](https://rebase.pro/docs/deployment/split-processes.md): Run one bundle as several cooperating processes — an API, a functions tier, a worker — from the same published runtime image, so a heavy custom function stops competing with the data API.
- [Running more than one instance](https://rebase.pro/docs/deployment/multiple-instances.md): Every piece of state a Rebase process keeps to itself, and the setting that shares it — what to set before a second replica, a rolling deploy or a split deployment takes traffic.
- [Running on an existing or shared database](https://rebase.pro/docs/deployment/existing-database.md): Run Rebase on a PostgreSQL database it does not own — a cluster shared with other apps, a second Rebase project, Supabase, or a database a DBA locks down — with the rls settings, rebase doctor --database and rebase db request-role migrate.
- [Backups and restore](https://rebase.pro/docs/deployment/backups.md): Take, schedule, list and restore database backups with pg_dump — what a backup contains, the roles file that travels with it, and the one thing it does not cover, your uploaded files.
- [Kubernetes](https://rebase.pro/docs/deployment/kubernetes.md): Deploy Rebase to a Kubernetes cluster with the official Helm chart — one Deployment or several, a migration Job that owns the schema, and static apps on the same host.
- [Deploying Rebase on AWS](https://rebase.pro/docs/deployment/aws.md): Deploy your Rebase instance securely on Amazon Web Services utilizing RDS and AWS App Runner with a strong European focus.
- [Deploying Rebase on Google Cloud Platform](https://rebase.pro/docs/deployment/gcp.md): Deploy your Rebase instance securely on GCP using Cloud SQL and Cloud Run, focusing on EU data center regions.
- [Deploying Rebase on Microsoft Azure](https://rebase.pro/docs/deployment/azure.md): Deploy your Rebase instance securely on Azure using Azure Database for PostgreSQL and Azure Container Apps.
- [Deploying Rebase on Hetzner Cloud](https://rebase.pro/docs/deployment/hetzner.md): Deploy a Rebase project on one Hetzner Cloud server with its own Docker Compose file and Caddy for HTTPS, or provision it with Terraform, for EU-based hosting.
- [Deploying Rebase on Scaleway](https://rebase.pro/docs/deployment/scaleway.md): Learn how to deploy Rebase on Scaleway for secure, French-based cloud infrastructure using Serverless Containers.
- [Deploying Rebase on Railway](https://rebase.pro/docs/deployment/railway.md): Deploy Rebase on Railway from the published runtime image and your project bundle. Maintain EU focus.
- [Deploying Rebase on Fly.io](https://rebase.pro/docs/deployment/flyio.md): Learn how to deploy Rebase globally or restrict it to European data centers using Fly.io.
- [Deploying Rebase on InstaPods](https://rebase.pro/docs/deployment/instapods.md): Take a fresh rebase init project to a live HTTPS URL on one InstaPods pod — Node, PostgreSQL and file uploads on the same machine, no Docker.
- [Deploying Rebase on Hostman](https://rebase.pro/docs/deployment/hostman.md): Deploy a rebase init project on Hostman — App Platform with Managed PostgreSQL and S3 storage, or one cloud server with your project's own Compose file.
- [Recipe: Blog CMS](https://rebase.pro/docs/recipes/blog-cms.md): Build a complete blog CMS with articles, authors, categories, rich text editing, and image uploads.
- [Recipe: Editorial publishing](https://rebase.pro/docs/recipes/editorial-publishing.md): Run a blog or newsroom on Rebase: writers and editors, review, scheduled publishing, drafts of live posts, previews, translations, a media library, content blocks, feeds, editorial notes and a WordPress import.
- [Recipe: Importing from WordPress](https://rebase.pro/docs/recipes/import-from-wordpress.md): Move posts from WordPress into Rebase with a script that reads the WordPress REST API and upserts each post by slug, so it can run again safely.
- [Recipe: Custom Dashboard](https://rebase.pro/docs/recipes/custom-dashboard.md): Build a dashboard page with KPI tiles and charts — numbers computed in SQL, drawn with the blocks from @rebasepro/ui.
- [Recipe: Webhook Integration](https://rebase.pro/docs/recipes/webhooks.md): Use entity callbacks to send webhooks to external services when data changes, without holding the write's transaction open.
